description: The only polling surface in the app. A self-refreshing fragment so the rest of the page (the form above it) does not rerun every 2 seconds along with the progress display.
signature:
@st.fragment(run_every='2s')
def render_progress_panel(db_path: Path, run_id: str) -> None
docstring:
Render live progress for one run and poll for updates.

Args:
    db_path: Opens its own short-lived connection inside this fragment call, per ADR-017 -- never receives or caches a connection from the caller.
    run_id: The run being watched.

Behavior:
    - with storage.connect(db_path) as conn: run = storage.get_run(conn, run_id); stages = storage.read_run_stages(conn, run_id); new_events = storage.read_run_events(conn, run_id, since_event_id=st.session_state['last_event_id']).
    - st.session_state['event_log'].extend(new_events); if new_events: st.session_state['last_event_id'] = new_events[-1].event_id.
    - Renders the stage list (acquisition/enrichment/analysis) with each stage's current status from stages, and the latest non-None progress value from event_log.
    - Renders a Cancel button calling orchestration.cancel_run(run_id), disabled once cancellation has already been requested this session (a local flag, not re-derived from server state, so the button visibly disables on the very next rerun rather than waiting for the worker to actually stop).
    - When run.status is a terminal value ('succeeded', 'failed', 'cancelled'): stop this fragment's own auto-refresh and call st.rerun() once, so the full page re-renders and (for the 'Run New Analysis' page specifically) can now show a link to the finished run's detail page instead of the live panel.
preconditions: st.session_state already has 'last_event_id' and 'event_log' initialized (by whichever page first set 'active_run_id')
postconditions: Each poll transfers only events newer than the previous high-water mark -- read_run_events is never called with since_event_id=0 on a second or later poll within the same run
The connection opened for this poll is closed before the fragment function returns
Once run.status is terminal, no further 2-second auto-refresh occurs for this fragment

edge_cases.input: The browser tab is refreshed mid-run (session_state reset)
edge_cases.expected_behavior: last_event_id resets to 0 (its declared default); the next poll re-reads the full run_events log from the start once, rebuilding event_log, then proceeds incrementally from there -- per the ui module spec's own edge case, this is expected and acceptable, not a bug

orchestration.cancel_run(run_id) is called once; the button is disabled immediately on this rerun via a local flag, even though the run's actual status has not yet changed (that happens asynchronously as the worker unwinds)

edge_cases.input: Cancel is pressed after the run already reached a terminal status
edge_cases.expected_behavior: cancel_run returns False; no error is shown, the terminal status is simply displayed as already-final

edge_cases.input: run_id no longer exists (should not normally happen once a panel is showing it, but defensively)
edge_cases.expected_behavior: storage.get_run returns None; the panel renders a 'run no longer found' state and stops polling, rather than raising

edge_cases.input: A multi-thousand-app run produces a very long event_log over a long session
edge_cases.expected_behavior: the panel renders a bounded tail (e.g. the last N entries) with the full log available in an expander, per the ui module spec's own edge case, so the page does not grow unbounded

unit_tests.name: test_incremental_read_advances_high_water_mark
unit_tests.description: Two successive polls each fetch only events newer than the previous poll's last event_id.
unit_tests.expected: second poll's read_run_events called with since_event_id equal to the first poll's max event_id

unit_tests.name: test_terminal_status_stops_polling
unit_tests.description: Once run.status becomes 'succeeded', the fragment's own refresh stops and st.rerun() is called once.
unit_tests.expected: no further scheduled refresh; st.rerun called exactly once

unit_tests.name: test_cancel_button_disabled_after_press
unit_tests.description: After Cancel is pressed once, the button renders disabled on the next call within the same session.

unit_tests.name: test_cancel_after_finished_is_noop
unit_tests.description: Pressing Cancel when the run already finished results in no error, cancel_run returning False.
unit_tests.expected: no exception, no state change beyond the button press

unit_tests.name: test_missing_run_shows_not_found_state
unit_tests.description: A run_id for which storage.get_run returns None renders a not-found message and does not raise.

unit_tests.name: test_connection_closed_after_each_poll
unit_tests.description: A connection-factory spy shows exactly one open/close pair per fragment invocation.
